a4_tas_mem.reason: gap=-4 (manual=14, measured=10), r/p/w clean. Definitively resolved Phase 171's own open arbitration question via direct trace of eu_req/grant_eu/grant_ifu/biu_cycle_gen state: grant_eu fires the very next tick after eu_req first asserts (tick174->175), zero IFU contention -- Phase 171's original 'mystery separate 16-tick bus cycle' hypothesis is disproven, not confirmed. The real, now fully-accounted-for breakdown: opcode fetch (2 clocks) + ordinary S0/S1 dispatch/setup latency (~2.5 clocks, same shape every instruction pays) + the locked read+write RMW cycle itself (6 clocks, continuously AS-asserted, confirmed pin-accurate). This RTL's own RMW dispatch computes TAS's read-then-decide-then-write sequence combinationally with no gap between the read completing and the write dispatching -- real 68030 microcode very likely needs genuine additional serial time to evaluate the read byte's own top bit before committing the write, the same 'internal microcode ceiling' character as the register-only dec_internal_stall_ticks_fixed cluster, just the first instance found in a bus-touching RMW instruction rather than a pure register op. Deliberately NOT fixed: dec_internal_stall_ticks_fixed only applies to register-only, non-bus-touching decode-time stalls; an analogous fix here would mean extending TAS's own locked RMW FSM (eu_seq.sv's tas_run_r/mem_rmw machinery) between the read ack and the write dispatch -- the same mechanism CAS/CAS2/BERR-abort protection (Phases 108-114) depend on being correct -- a disproportionate correctness risk for a single -4 gap on a comparatively rare instruction
a4_tas_mem.ref: plan.md Phase 171 (original investigation) and timing-gaps-largest-first plan Stage 2 (definitive resolution)

a2_move_rn_anind.reason: gap=+2 (manual=4, measured=6), r/p/w clean. This RTL's own plain-write BIU dispatch has a shared, EA-mode-independent ~6-clock floor -- confirmed exact for CLR.L (a0) (manual=6 including its own explicit cea((An))=2 addition, measured=6). MOVE Rn,(An)'s own manual row is self-contained at NCC=4 with NO cea/fea addition (unlike CLR's row), implying real 68030 microcode genuinely executes MOVE's own EA-then-write sequence 2 clocks faster than CLR's -- a genuine per-instruction microcode difference this project's shared, uniform write-dispatch path can't distinguish. Can't be fixed by shrinking the shared floor (would break CLR's own currently-exact measurement) or via dec_internal_stall_ticks_fixed (that mechanism only applies to register-only, non-bus-touching instructions) without a genuinely new, instruction-specific dispatch-latency mechanism -- same architectural-ceiling character as the briefidx cases above
